title: Learning Theories — Quick Revision
keyConcepts: Behaviourism: learning = observable change in behaviour through stimulus–response (Pavlov, Thorndike, Skinner, Watson)
Cognitivism: learning = mental processing, insight, schema (Piaget, Bruner, Gestalt — Köhler, Wertheimer)
Constructivism: learner actively builds knowledge (Piaget — cognitive; Vygotsky — social)
Social learning: observation, imitation, modelling (Bandura)
Humanism: whole person, needs, self-actualisation (Maslow, Rogers)

theories.name: Pavlov — Classical Conditioning
points: Classroom: pleasant associations with school/subjects reduce anxiety

theories.name: Thorndike — Trial & Error / Connectionism
points: Secondary laws: multiple response, attitude, analogy, associative shifting

theories.name: Skinner — Operant Conditioning
points: Positive/negative reinforcement (↑ behaviour); positive/negative punishment (↓ behaviour)

theories.name: Köhler — Insight (Gestalt)
points: Whole > sum of parts; laws of perception (similarity, proximity, closure)

theories.name: Piaget — Cognitive Development
points: Sensorimotor 0–2 (object permanence); Pre-operational 2–7 (egocentrism, animism, no conservation); Concrete operational 7–11 (conservation, reversibility, classification, seriation); Formal 11+ (abstract, hypothetical)

theories.name: Bruner — Discovery Learning
points: Modes of representation: enactive → iconic → symbolic (basis of CPA)
Spiral curriculum; 'any subject can be taught at any age in an intellectually honest form'

theories.name: Kohlberg — Moral Development
points: Pre-conventional (punishment-obedience; instrumental), Conventional (good boy/girl; law & order), Post-conventional (social contract; universal ethics)

theories.name: Erikson — Psychosocial
points: Trust vs mistrust (0–1); Autonomy vs shame (1–3); Initiative vs guilt (3–6); Industry vs inferiority (6–12) ← primary school; Identity vs role confusion (12–18)

educators.name: Maria Montessori
educators.contribution: Sensory training, didactic apparatus, prepared environment, 'Children's House'

educators.name: Friedrich Froebel
educators.contribution: Kindergarten (1837), play, 'gifts and occupations', 'father of kindergarten'

educators.name: John Dewey
educators.contribution: Learning by doing, pragmatism, school as miniature society, 'Democracy and Education'

educators.name: Howard Gardner
educators.contribution: Multiple Intelligences (8): linguistic, logical-mathematical, spatial, musical, bodily-kinaesthetic, interpersonal, intrapersonal, naturalistic

educators.name: Benjamin Bloom
educators.contribution: Taxonomy of educational objectives — cognitive (remember, understand, apply, analyse, evaluate, create — revised 2001), affective, psychomotor

examPoints: Positive = add; negative = remove; reinforcement ↑; punishment ↓
Primary school children (6–11) → concrete operational (Piaget), industry vs inferiority (Erikson), pre-conventional/conventional (Kohlberg)
Piaget = cognitive constructivism; Vygotsky = social constructivism
Thorndike's Law of Effect → basis of Skinner's reinforcement
Gardner's MI → differentiated teaching; Sternberg → triarchic (analytical, creative, practical)
commonTraps: Attributing 'ZPD' to Piaget or 'schema' to Vygotsky
Thinking Kohlberg gave psychosocial stages (that's Erikson)
Bruner's spiral curriculum vs Piaget's stages

title: Growth, Development & Individual Differences
keyConcepts: Growth = quantitative (height, weight); Development = qualitative + quantitative, lifelong
Principles: continuity, sequential, general→specific, cephalocaudal, proximodistal, individual differences, heredity×environment, predictable pattern, integration
Stages: infancy (0–2), early childhood (2–6), later childhood (6–12), adolescence (12–18)
Factors: heredity (genes), environment (nutrition, family, SES, school, peers, media, culture), maturation and learning interplay
Individual differences: intelligence, aptitude, interest, attitude, learning style, personality, SES, gender, language
examPoints: Later childhood (6–12) = 'gang age', 'elementary school age', 'pseudo-maturity' (Hurlock)
Adolescence = 'period of storm and stress' (Stanley Hall)
Intelligence: Binet — mental age; IQ = MA/CA × 100 (Terman); Spearman g-factor; Thurstone primary abilities; Guilford SI model
Normal IQ 90–109; gifted ≥ 130 (varies by scale)

title: Special Provisions for Divyang (CWSN) Students
keyConcepts: RPwD Act 2016: 21 disabilities; replaces PwD Act 1995 (7); 4% reservation in govt jobs, 5% in higher education; inclusive education Sec. 16–17; reasonable accommodation
Specific Learning Disabilities: dyslexia (reading), dysgraphia (writing), dyscalculia (maths), dyspraxia (motor)
ASD, ADHD (not separately listed in RPwD but supported), intellectual disability, cerebral palsy, hearing/visual/speech impairment, locomotor
Models: charity → medical → social → rights-based; segregation → integration → inclusion
IEP (Individualised Education Plan); resource room; special educator; UDL (Universal Design for Learning)
Samagra Shiksha (2018): inclusive education component — aids, appliances, escort/transport allowance, home-based education
NEP 2020 Chapter 6: SEDGs; special educators; Divyang-friendly infrastructure
CBSE exemptions/relaxations: extra time, scribe, calculator (dyscalculia), alternative subjects
examPoints: PwD Act 1995 → 7 categories; RPwD 2016 → 21
Braille — Louis Braille; Braille Day 4 January; White Cane Day 15 October; International Day of Persons with Disabilities 3 December
Accessible India Campaign (Sugamya Bharat Abhiyan) 2015
Sign language: ISLRTC (2015), Indian Sign Language dictionary

title: NEP 2020, NCF & New Initiatives — Fact Sheet
keyConcepts: NEP 2020: approved 29 July 2020; Kasturirangan committee (draft 2019); replaces NPE 1986/1992; MHRD renamed Ministry of Education
5+3+3+4: Foundational (3–8: 3 yrs pre-school + Cl 1–2), Preparatory (8–11: Cl 3–5), Middle (11–14: Cl 6–8), Secondary (14–18: Cl 9–12)
Goals: 100% GER in school by 2030; 6% GDP on education; FLN by Grade 3; universal ECCE; mother tongue till Grade 5 (preferably 8)
Teachers: 4-year ITEP by 2030; 50 hrs CPD/year; NPST (National Professional Standards for Teachers); TET for all stages
Assessment: PARAKH; Holistic Progress Card; board exams twice a year, low stakes; exams in Grades 3, 5, 8

Curriculum: reduce to core essentials; no hard separation of arts/science, curricular/co-curricular, vocational/academic; coding from Class 6; vocational exposure & internships from Class 6; bagless days
Frameworks: NCF-FS (Oct 2022), NCF-SE (Aug 2023); NCF for ECCE and Teacher Education pending/ongoing

theories.name: NIPUN Bharat (5 July 2021)
points: Lakshya per grade; 3 developmental goals (health & well-being; effective communicators; involved learners)

theories.name: DIKSHA / PM eVIDYA / NISHTHA
points: PM eVIDYA 2020 — one nation one digital platform, 12 TV channels (one class one channel)

theories.name: Other
points: ULLAS — Nav Bharat Saaksharta Karyakram (adult literacy)
APAAR ID — Automated Permanent Academic Account Registry (One Nation One Student ID)

examPoints: Kothari Commission 1964–66: 10+2+3, 6% GDP, common school system
NPE 1986 → POA 1992: Operation Blackboard, Navodaya Vidyalayas, DIET
Yashpal Committee 1993 'Learning Without Burden' → NCF 2005
NCF 2005: five guiding principles — connect knowledge to life, shift from rote, enrich curriculum beyond textbooks, flexible exams, democratic polity
Chattopadhyaya Commission 1983–85 (teachers); Justice Verma Commission 2012 (teacher education)

title: Measurement & Evaluation Essentials
keyConcepts: Measurement = assigning numbers; Assessment = gathering evidence; Evaluation = value judgement
Formative (for learning, during) vs Summative (of learning, end); Diagnostic (before/identify gaps); Placement; Prognostic
Norm-referenced (compare to group) vs Criterion-referenced (compare to standard)
Qualities of a good test: validity, reliability, objectivity, usability, comprehensiveness, discriminating power
CCE (RTE Sec. 29) — scholastic + co-scholastic; NEP → HPC, 360°
Tools: observation, checklist, rating scale, anecdotal record, portfolio, rubric, oral test, project, cumulative record
Bloom's revised taxonomy for question setting; Learning Outcomes (NCERT 2017)
examPoints: Validity types: content, construct, criterion (predictive/concurrent), face
Reliability methods: test-retest, parallel forms, split-half, KR-20
A reliable test may not be valid; a valid test is always reliable
Grading vs marking; absolute vs relative grading
commonTraps: Formative ≠ 'frequent tests' — it must feed back into teaching

title: Teaching Methods, Skills & Lesson Planning
keyConcepts: Maxims of teaching: known→unknown, simple→complex, concrete→abstract, particular→general, whole→part, psychological→logical, induction→deduction, analysis→synthesis

Methods: lecture, demonstration, discussion, play-way, activity, project (Kilpatrick), problem-solving, heuristic (Armstrong), inductive-deductive, Dalton plan (Parkhurst), Montessori, Kindergarten (Froebel), storytelling, dramatisation
Micro-teaching (Allen & Ryan, Stanford 1963): 5–10 min, 5–10 pupils, one skill; cycle plan→teach→feedback→re-plan→re-teach→re-feedback
Core skills: set induction, questioning (probing), explaining, illustrating with examples, stimulus variation, reinforcement, blackboard writing, closure
Herbartian steps: preparation, presentation, comparison/association, generalisation, application, (recapitulation)
Bloom's objectives; Learning outcomes; TLM — audio, visual, audio-visual; Edgar Dale's Cone of Experience
Lesson plan approaches: Herbartian, Morrison (unit), Bloom (evaluation), RCEM, constructivist 5E (engage, explore, explain, elaborate, evaluate)
examPoints: Project method — Kilpatrick; Heuristic — H.E. Armstrong; Dalton — Helen Parkhurst; Kindergarten — Froebel; Montessori — Maria Montessori; Basic education (Nai Talim) — Gandhi (Wardha 1937)
Team teaching — Harvard; Programmed learning — Skinner; Discovery learning — Bruner
Inductive: examples → rule; Deductive: rule → examples

title: Life Skills, Motivation, Values & Teacher Roles
keyConcepts: WHO 10 life skills: self-awareness, empathy, critical thinking, creative thinking, decision making, problem solving, effective communication, interpersonal relationships, coping with stress, coping with emotions

Motivation: intrinsic vs extrinsic; Maslow's hierarchy (physiological, safety, love/belonging, esteem, self-actualisation; later cognitive, aesthetic, transcendence); McClelland — achievement, power, affiliation; Weiner — attribution; Deci & Ryan — SDT (autonomy, competence, relatedness); Atkinson — achievement motivation
Teacher roles: facilitator, monitor/observer, leader, guide, counsellor, mentor, reflective practitioner (NCF 2005)
Professional ethics: NCTE Code of Professional Ethics (2010); CCS Conduct Rules; KVS Education Code; no private tuition of own students; impartiality; confidentiality; child protection (POCSO 2012)
Constitutional values: Preamble — justice, liberty, equality, fraternity; secularism; democracy; Fundamental Duties Art. 51-A (11); dignity
Reward & punishment: reinforcement > punishment; RTE Sec. 17 bans corporal punishment; NCPCR guidelines 2012; positive discipline; logical consequences; token economy
examPoints: Maslow: 'deficiency needs' vs 'growth needs'
Extrinsic rewards can undermine intrinsic motivation (over-justification effect)
Adolescence & life skills education — NCERT/CBSE life skills manuals
Value education: NCERT 'Education for Values in Schools — A Framework' (2012)

title: ICT in Education — Platforms & Concepts
keyConcepts: Government platforms: DIKSHA (2017, OER, QR), SWAYAM (MOOCs), SWAYAM PRABHA (DTH channels), e-Pathshala (NCERT textbooks app), NROER (National Repository of OER, 2013), NISHTHA (teacher training), PM eVIDYA (2020), ePG Pathshala (PG), NDLI (National Digital Library, IIT-KGP), Vidya Daan, ShaGun portal, UDISE+, PRERNA (UP), APAAR ID
OER: openly licensed (Creative Commons) teaching-learning resources — 5Rs: retain, reuse, revise, remix, redistribute
Computer basics: hardware/software; input/output/storage; CPU (ALU, CU, registers); RAM (volatile) vs ROM; units bit→byte→KB→MB→GB→TB; OS (Windows, Android, Linux); MS Office basics; file types
Internet: WWW (Berners-Lee 1989), URL, HTTP/HTTPS, browser, search engine, email, cloud, Wi-Fi, IP address; ISP
Smartphone/apps for teaching: Google Classroom, video conferencing, e-content, QR scanners; digital TLM — PPT, videos, simulations (PhET), interactive whiteboards
Frameworks: TPACK (Mishra & Koehler), SAMR (Puentedura), blended learning, flipped classroom
Digital safety: cyber-bullying, passwords, privacy; IT Act 2000; Cyber Crime portal 1930
Digital India (2015): pillars incl. e-Kranti; BharatNet; Bhashini
examPoints: DIKSHA = Digital Infrastructure for Knowledge Sharing
SWAYAM = Study Webs of Active-Learning for Young Aspiring Minds
1 byte = 8 bits; 1 KB = 1024 bytes
Father of computer — Charles Babbage; first Indian supercomputer — PARAM 8000 (C-DAC, 1991)

title: Mathematics — Formula & Shortcut Sheet
keyConcepts: Percentage: x% of y = xy/100; successive change a, b → a + b + ab/100; % increase then equal % decrease → net −(x²/100)%
Profit/Loss on CP: P% = (SP−CP)/CP × 100; SP = CP(100±x)/100; discount on MP
SI = PRT/100; CI: A = P(1 + R/100)ⁿ; CI − SI (2 yrs) = P(R/100)²
Average = sum/n; weighted average; average of consecutive numbers = (first + last)/2
Ratio: a:b, b:c → a:b:c; proportion a/b = c/d ⇒ ad = bc; direct vs inverse variation
HCF × LCM = product of two numbers; LCM of fractions = LCM(num)/HCF(den)
Divisibility rules 2–11; prime numbers < 50; squares to 30, cubes to 12
Identities: (a±b)² = a² ± 2ab + b²; a² − b² = (a+b)(a−b); (a+b)³ = a³ + b³ + 3ab(a+b); a³ + b³ = (a+b)(a² − ab + b²); x + 1/x = k ⇒ x² + 1/x² = k² − 2
Area: rectangle lb; square a²; triangle ½bh; Heron √(s(s−a)(s−b)(s−c)); parallelogram bh; rhombus ½d₁d₂; trapezium ½(a+b)h; circle πr², circumference 2πr
Volume/Surface: cube a³/6a²; cuboid lbh / 2(lb+bh+hl); cylinder πr²h / 2πr(r+h); cone ⅓πr²h; sphere 4/3πr³ / 4πr²; 1 m³ = 1000 L
Geometry: angle sum triangle 180°, polygon (n−2)180°, exterior angles sum 360°; Pythagoras; types of triangles/quadrilaterals; circle terms
Statistics: mean, median (middle of sorted), mode (most frequent); range; bar graph, pictograph, pie chart (360° = total)
Time-work: work = rate × time; unitary method; speed = distance/time; km/h → m/s ×5/18
examPoints: Place value vs face value
Fraction comparison: cross-multiply or LCM
BODMAS order
Roman numerals I V X L C D M
commonTraps: Profit % on SP instead of CP

title: हिन्दी व्याकरण — परीक्षा-केंद्रित बिंदु
keyConcepts: वर्ण: स्वर 11 (अ आ इ ई उ ऊ ए ऐ ओ औ + ऋ), व्यंजन 33 (+ ड़ ढ़ = 35; संयुक्त क्ष त्र ज्ञ श्र); अयोगवाह — अनुस्वार, विसर्ग
संधि: स्वर (दीर्घ, गुण, वृद्धि, यण्, अयादि), व्यंजन, विसर्ग — उदाहरण याद करें
समास: अव्ययीभाव (यथाशक्ति), तत्पुरुष (राजपुत्र), कर्मधारय (चंद्रमुख), द्विगु (त्रिलोक), द्वंद्व (माता-पिता), बहुव्रीहि (दशानन)
उपसर्ग (अ, अन, अति, अधि, अनु, अभि, प्र, परा, सु, दुर्…) और प्रत्यय (कृत्, तद्धित)
शब्द भेद: तत्सम, तद्भव, देशज, विदेशज; पर्यायवाची, विलोम, अनेकार्थी, एकार्थी, श्रुतिसमभिन्नार्थक
वाक्य: रचना के आधार पर सरल/संयुक्त/मिश्र; अर्थ के आधार पर 8 प्रकार; वाच्य (कर्तृ, कर्म, भाव)

title: Indian Constitution & Governance — Must-Know
keyConcepts: Constituent Assembly: first meeting 9 Dec 1946; President Rajendra Prasad; Drafting Committee chair B.R. Ambedkar (29 Aug 1947); adopted 26 Nov 1949; in force 26 Jan 1950; originally 395 Articles, 22 Parts, 8 Schedules (now 12 Schedules)
Preamble: Sovereign Socialist Secular Democratic Republic; Justice Liberty Equality Fraternity (42nd Amendment 1976 added Socialist, Secular, Integrity)
Fundamental Rights Part III Art. 12–35: Equality 14–18, Freedom 19–22, against Exploitation 23–24 (child labour <14 in hazardous jobs), Religion 25–28, Cultural & Educational 29–30, Remedies 32
Art. 21-A RTE (86th Amdt 2002); Art. 45 ECCE; Art. 46 SC/ST education; Art. 350-A mother tongue instruction at primary; Art. 351 Hindi
DPSP Part IV (36–51); Fundamental Duties Part IV-A Art. 51-A (11 duties)
Union: President (Art. 52), PM & Council of Ministers (74–75), Parliament (Lok Sabha 543 elected, Rajya Sabha 245); Judiciary — Supreme Court (Art. 124)
State: Governor (153), CM (164), Legislature; High Court
Local: 73rd (Panchayats, 1992) & 74th (Municipalities) Amendments; 11th & 12th Schedules
Education on Concurrent List since 42nd Amendment (1976)
examPoints: Constitution Day 26 Nov; Republic Day 26 Jan; Law Day
Longest written constitution; borrowed features (UK — parliamentary; USA — FRs, judicial review; Ireland — DPSP; Canada — federation with strong centre)
UP: 80 Lok Sabha seats; 403 Assembly seats; 100 Legislative Council seats (bicameral); 75 districts, 18 divisions
commonTraps: Art. 45 changed by 86th Amendment to ECCE (0–6)

title: Uttar Pradesh — Static GK Snapshot
keyConcepts: Formation: United Provinces → Uttar Pradesh 24 Jan 1950 (UP Diwas); Uttarakhand carved out 9 Nov 2000

Capital Lucknow; High Court Prayagraj (Allahabad HC, 1866, oldest HC in India after Calcutta/Bombay/Madras… est. 1866 at Agra, moved 1869) with Lucknow bench; 75 districts, 18 divisions; most populous state; largest Lok Sabha seats (80)
Symbols: animal — barasingha (swamp deer); bird — sarus crane; tree — ashoka; flower — palash; dance — kathak; sport — hockey
Rivers: Ganga, Yamuna, Ghaghara, Gomti, Ramganga, Betwa, Ken, Son, Sharda, Rapti, Chambal
Wildlife: Dudhwa NP (Lakhimpur Kheri) & Dudhwa Tiger Reserve, Pilibhit TR, Amangarh TR, Ranipur TR; sanctuaries — Chandra Prabha, National Chambal, Nawabganj/Shahid Chandra Shekhar Azad, Okhla
Heritage: Taj Mahal, Agra Fort, Fatehpur Sikri (UNESCO); Sarnath, Kushinagar, Shravasti (Buddhist circuit); Ayodhya, Varanasi, Mathura-Vrindavan, Prayagraj (Kumbh)
Schemes: ODOP (2018), Mission Prerna/NIPUN (basic education), Kanya Sumangala, Abhyudaya coaching, Vishwakarma Shram Samman; UP GIS; expressways (Purvanchal, Bundelkhand, Ganga Expressway)
Education bodies: UPESSC (Prayagraj), UP Basic Education Board (Prayagraj), UPMSP (Board, Prayagraj), SCERT Lucknow, DIETs

Personalities: Premchand, Tulsidas, Kabir, Surdas, Jaishankar Prasad, Mahadevi Verma, Nirala, Bismillah Khan, Birju Maharaj, Ravi Shankar; freedom fighters — Mangal Pandey, Rani Lakshmibai (Jhansi), Chandrashekhar Azad (Prayagraj), Ram Prasad Bismil, Ashfaqulla Khan (Kakori 1925)
Folk: Nautanki, Ramlila, Raslila, Kajri, Birha, Chaiti; fairs — Kumbh, Bateshwar, Dev Deepawali

Chauri Chaura 1922 (Gorakhpur)
Kakori 1925
